hook_text: One line, twelve bars. In ten seconds you can tell winter rain from summer rain.
clip_script: Here is a climate graph. Along the bottom: the months. The line: how warm it usually is. The bars: how much rain usually falls. Now the trick. Look where the tallest bars are, and check the line above them. Station A: tall bars in June and July, right under the lowest part of the line. Rain when it is cool: winter rain, a Mediterranean climate like Cape Town, five hundred and fifteen millimetres a year. Station B: tall bars from October to March, under the highest part of the line. Rain when it is hot: summer rain, like Pretoria, with only three millimetres in July. Range? Highest minus lowest. Total? Add the bars. Done.
visual_style: A whiteboard climate graph drawn live, a finger tracing from the tallest bar up to the line, then a second graph flipping the pattern.
mood: Quick, confident, like a skill trick.
pacing: Snappy steps with a counter ticking to ten seconds.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and practise reading graphs like a pro.
